hooks.text: Your Sunday plan hits different than your Tuesday self.
Why does Wednesday always feel like starting over?
The psychology your planner won't tell you about.
Your timetable doesn't fail. Your brain chemistry does.
Sunday you and Tuesday you aren't the same person.
That perfect schedule lasted exactly 36 hours, right?
You're not lazy. Your Sunday brain is just lying.
Every Monday you're unstoppable. By Wednesday you're a ghost.
Plot twist: your schedule didn't fail, science did.
Stop blaming yourself. It's literally neurobiology, not discipline.

winner.text: Your Sunday plan hits different than your Tuesday self.
winner.reasoning: This hook mirrors the exact lived experience of procrastinating college students—they *feel* the Monday-to-Tuesday shift viscerally but can't name it. The phrase 'hits different' is authentically Gen-Z casual and creates immediate recognition without being preachy. It's intrinsically relatable enough to stop scroll without needing to explain why they should care.

runner_up.text: You're not lazy. Your Sunday brain is just lying.
runner_up.reasoning: Directly addresses the shame and self-blame that procrastinators carry while offering implicit permission to reframe the problem. Slightly safer because it centers on absolution rather than curiosity, making it broadly appealing even to less self-aware viewers.

script.script:
[HOOK - 0-3 sec]
"Your Sunday plan hits different than your Tuesday self."
[PAUSE]

[PROBLEM - 3-8 sec]
"You map out this perfect week on Sunday. Tasks organized, time blocked, motivation is HIGH."
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Sunday You: Unstoppable]
"Then Tuesday hits and... who is that person? They're gone."
[CUT]

[VALUE - 8-20 sec]
"Here's what actually works: stop planning for Future You. Plan for Tired You."
[PAUSE]
"Build buffers. Make tasks stupidly small. Use the 2-minute rule—if it takes less than 2 minutes, do it NOW."
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: 2-Min Rule = No Excuses]
"Tuesday You won't have motivation, but Tuesday You will have a system."
[CUT]

[CTA - 20-22 sec]
"Follow for the full system that actually survives past Wednesday."
[PAUSE]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Follow for more]
script.viewer_takeaway: Planning fails because we overestimate our future motivation. The 2-minute rule and buffer-building create a system that works for tired, unmotivated you—not hypothetical ideal you.

cover_options: Split-screen: left side shows organized planner/calendar (bright, energetic); right side shows tired person in bed with pillow over head. Bold text overlay: 'Sunday You vs Tuesday You'
Close-up of someone's face looking confident and motivated (Sunday), then instantly switches to same person looking exhausted and confused (Tuesday). Text: 'The Plot Twist'

frame_plan.visual_direction: Split-screen comparison: left = person at desk with planner, energetic lighting, coffee in hand, smiling; right = same person disheveled in bed or slouched at desk looking lost. Quick cuts between them.
Close-up of digital calendar or planner being filled out with tasks, color-coded sections, satisfying time-blocking visuals. Upbeat energy.
Person looking confident, pumped-up pose (fist bump, thumbs up). Quick transition to messy desk, person rubbing face in confusion. Text pops: 'Where did I go?'
Person yawning, stretching in bed, looking unmotivated. Text appears as voiceover delivers solution. Transition to visual of simplified task list on notepad (fewer items, bigger spacing).
Montage of quick wins: person doing small tasks rapidly (2-3 sec clips each). Timer graphic appears showing '2:00'. Satisfying task-completion checkmarks on screen.
Same person on Tuesday, now calm and executing. Showing them checking off tasks methodically, moving through day with ease. Show calendar/system working smoothly in background.
Person gives knowing nod or slight smile at camera. Follow button animation pops up on screen. Soft background showing organized workspace/system.

justifications.clarity: Hook lands instantly with relatable contrast; problem-value structure is linear and easy to follow.
justifications.retention: Strong opening with visual flip-flop keeps eyes moving, but value section (8-20s) risks feeling like generic productivity advice without differentiation.
justifications.save_potential: Practical tactics (2-min rule, buffer-building) are immediately applicable; worth a save for reference.
justifications.shareability: Relatability is high, but post doesn't create urgency or novelty—feels familiar to existing productivity content.
justifications.audience_fit: Procrastinating college students will viscerally recognize Sunday-vs-Tuesday gap; addresses their exact failure pattern.
justifications.cta_strength: Follow-for-more is passive; no sense of what 'the system' is or why Tuesday will be different by following.

weaknesses.issue: CTA is vague ('follow for the full system') without teasing what that system actually delivers or why Tuesday matters.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite to: 'Follow for the exact Tuesday checklist that survives past Wednesday—no motivation required.' (Adds specificity and reinforces the differentiation.)

weaknesses.issue: Value section (8-20s) delivers three tactics (buffers, small tasks, 2-min rule) but doesn't show *why* these beat Sunday planning—feels like stacked tips instead of a unified philosophy.
weaknesses.fix: Restructure: 'Stop fighting your Tuesday brain. Give it a system so simple motivation doesn't matter. The 2-minute rule? You do it NOW, not later. Buffers? Built in. Tasks? Stupidly small.' (Unifies tactics around the core idea: system replaces motivation.)

weaknesses.issue: Visual climax at 16-20s (person calmly executing Tuesday) doesn't show the *contrast* with their panicked Sunday-self—moment to anchor the win is underutilized.
weaknesses.fix: Split-screen finale: left side = Tuesday person looking calm/composed executing tasks; right side = quick flash of chaotic Sunday-planner energy; text: 'Same person. Different system.' (Pays off the opening contrast and proves the method works.)

captions: Sunday You has a plan. Tuesday You has amnesia. 📋➡️😴 The difference? Stop planning for Future You. Plan for Tired You. Build buffers. Use the 2-min rule. Let the system do the work motivation can't. Follow for the exact Tuesday playbook that actually survives past Wednesday.

Your perfect Sunday plan lasted until Tuesday lunch. 😅 Here's the fix: quit relying on motivation and build a system for your exhausted brain instead. The 2-min rule, micro-tasks, built-in buffers—these aren't motivational tips, they're Tuesday armor. Follow for the system that wins when willpower dies.
growth.final_call_reason: Strong hook and audience fit, but CTA is too weak (no specificity on what follows delivers), value section stacks generic advice instead of unified philosophy, and visual payoff doesn't reinforce the Sunday-vs-Tuesday contrast—fix these three and this becomes post-worthy.
